name: Botox brow lift

lead: A botulinum toxin brow lift uses small injections to weaken muscles that pull the eyebrow down, letting the outer brow rest higher. It is discussed in looksmaxxing forums as a reversible alternative to surgical brow lifts.
The effect is temporary. A small case series and several registered Phase 4 trials have examined toxin for brow elevation.

paras: Botulinum toxin type A relaxes the muscles it is injected into. Weakening brow depressors relative to the forehead muscle that lifts the brow can raise the brow position.

Reported side effects of cosmetic toxin include brow or eyelid drooping, bruising, headaches, spread of the toxin effect and, rarely, double vision. The FDA added boxed warnings about toxin spread in 2009. Botox Cosmetic is approved for glabellar lines; brow lifting is not a labeled use.

lead: A botulinum toxin brow lift is a non-surgical technique in which small injections weaken muscles that pull the eyebrow down, letting the outer brow sit higher. Botox is the best-known brand; Dysport and others are also used.[1]

In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to 'lift the tails' of the brows and open the eye area without surgery. Published research includes a 2000 case series on temporal brow elevation with botulinum toxin and several registered trials of toxin for brow position.[2]

Effects are temporary. Wikipedia reports that cosmetic toxin effects typically last two to four months for glabellar lines, and brow or eyelid drooping is listed among reported side effects of some products.[3]

Brow or eyelid drooping, bruising, spread of toxin effect

paras: Botulinum toxin type A relaxes the muscles it is injected into. The forehead's frontalis muscle lifts the brow, while the corrugator, procerus and the orbicularis oculi pull it down. Injecting depressor muscles more than the frontalis can allow the brow, especially its outer part, to rest higher. Wikipedia notes that brow elevation after toxin was first noticed in an unplanned case reported in 1989 in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery.[3]

A prospective case series of 22 cosmetic patients tested whether paralysis of brow depressors after botulinum toxin A injection raised the brow. Registered trials include Phase 4 studies of Dysport for brow lifting (24 participants) and of toxin and brow height or morphology (including a randomized controlled trial of 30 participants), and a study combining microfocused ultrasound, abobotulinumtoxinA and temporal filler for non-surgical brow lifting.[2][4][5][6]

Wikipedia's article on botulinum toxin lists brow and eyelid drooping as common side effects of some newer products, and notes that toxin can spread from the injection site or reach the wrong muscle, causing weakness. Bruising, headaches and allergic reactions are also reported, and temporary double vision has been described in a few cases. In 2009 the FDA announced boxed warnings about distant spread of toxin effects.[3]
Forum participants describe botulinum toxin as a reversible way to adjust brow shape, including threads on a "reverse brow lift" approach.

The 2000 case series of 22 patients examined brow elevation after botulinum toxin A. Registered trials include NCT01401803 (Dysport, Phase 4, completed),[2] NCT01308593 (Brow Enhancement Study, Phase 4, 30 participants, completed),[4] NCT02942303 (randomized trial of toxin on brow height and morphology, status unknown),[6] NCT03186001 (frontalis toxin, status unknown),[7] and NCT07894822 (combined ultrasound, toxin and filler for brow lifting, completed).[5] Published results of the registered trials were not located in the sources consulted.

lore.intro: Botulinum toxin is discussed as a reversible, lower-commitment way to adjust brow shape.

claims.claim: Botox can lift the brow tails without surgery

timeline.event: Case report in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery describes brow elevation as an unintended effect of toxin, considered the first described aesthetic use.[3]
Case series of temporal brow lift using botulinum toxin A is published.
FDA approves Botox Cosmetic for glabellar lines.[3]
Phase 4 trials of Dysport for brow lifting and brow enhancement begin.[2][4]
